scope: 20 Week 4 core features and six mandatory Week 7 changes; test intent reviewed, final acceptance remains human-owned.

sources.title: Sprint 4 scope and Definition of Done

requirements.name: Authentication and authorisation
requirements.intent: Password login resolves the stored role; record ownership and role restrict actions. Registered attendee membership cannot grant lifecycle mutation or internal fields.
gaps: Production HTTPS/cookie deployment and browser inactivity expiry need release-environment evidence. SCRUM-141 now uses an atomic failed-login RPC and adds persisted recovery tests; simultaneous login-failure evidence remains a separate concurrency check.

requirements.name: Event request creation
requirements.intent: Required request details are validated; valid submission persists with actor attribution, invalid submission leaves the draft unchanged.

requirements.name: Draft event requests
requirements.intent: An incomplete private draft can be saved, reopened and submitted once using the same event reference.

requirements.name: Event review and approval
requirements.intent: Only the assigned Coordinator approves/rejects a submitted request; rejection requires a reason and the Organiser receives the outcome. Clarification supports revision/resubmission.
gaps: INTEGRATED-11 proves clarification, same-request resubmission and persisted rejection in the real browser/API/database lane. Clarification source conflict J2 and section-specific acceptance still require owner confirmation.

requirements.name: Coordinator assignment and reassignment
requirements.intent: Submission enters an unassigned queue. The Lead assigns/reassigns; prior Coordinator loses action access; recipients and stored membership follow the assignment.

requirements.name: Event status management
requirements.intent: Status presentation follows the actor; confirmation, safety and completion have dedicated gates; attendees cannot mutate lifecycle.
gaps: The SCRUM-135 role/state matrix is implemented and real-database tested. SCRUM-161 adds browser evidence for read-only controls and unrelated-role denial. Related venue/technical staff retain existing planning read permissions; attendee public projection and no internal payload in denied mutation responses are separate assertions. Final policy acceptance remains human-owned.

requirements.name: Event information management
requirements.intent: Planning edits preserve attribution and become read-only after confirmation. Important changes need reconsideration of existing resource arrangements.

checks.test: the propose-values panel gives the venue options their own full-width rows
keeps the venue options out of the grid that lays out the simple fields

gaps: SCRUM-138/152/156/48/166 apply significant changes, preserve resources and return Confirmed/Preparation date changes to Planning. Other significant changes remain flag-only under D36/D43/D64; final policy acceptance remains human-owned.

requirements.name: Venue catalogue
requirements.intent: Venue details persist, duplicates and invalid capacities are rejected, updates preserve booking records and audit, and an opened venue shows its full record.

checks.test: shows the complete catalogue record, not only name location and capacity
lists the opening hours of every day, including the days the venue is closed
marks a venue that is closed right now, naming the reason and when it reopens
offers a Coordinator no way to change the venue
reports a retired venue as retired even while a closure is running

requirements.name: Venue availability calendar
requirements.intent: Internal users see occupied booking intervals and maintenance in the calendar; maintenance remains visible over existing confirmed occupation. Half-open occupied boundaries remain compatible.

checks.test: coordinator sees the availability calendar with a confirmed slot

requirements.name: Venue search and filtering
requirements.intent: Combined filters run before pagination, reject malformed slots, and never claim availability when database reads fail.
gaps: Availability is evaluated at read time; a later competing booking can still produce an honest conflict on submission. R1/R5 SQL concurrency checks cover enforcement, not a reservation guarantee from a search result.

requirements.name: Venue suitability checking
requirements.intent: Capacity, layout, facilities and accessibility contribute independent suitability flags, including exact capacity and missing-data boundaries.
gaps: TC-29-04 advisory suitability versus booking hard capacity gate needs section-specific acceptance reconciliation.

requirements.name: Venue booking request
requirements.intent: An assigned Coordinator submits independent bookings for one event. Editing/cancelling one booking must preserve its sibling and parent; persistence failures must not report success.

checks.test: Coordinator changes one Requested booking and the changes survive reopening

gaps: SCRUM-166 now checks approved venue union coverage and equipment reservation timing at confirmation. Audit A1/A2 remain: expired holds block confirmation, and booking cancellation after confirmation does not invalidate readiness before safety approval.

requirements.name: Venue booking approval
requirements.intent: Venue Staff approve/reject with reasons, confirmation affects availability, and a competing confirmed booking blocks approval.

requirements.name: Booking conflict detection
requirements.intent: Half-open boundaries, confirmed/blocked precedence and tentative holds prevent incompatible booking requests.
gaps: Audit A3 (3 November 2026): increasing buffers can introduce a conflict with pre-existing maintenance without identifying/notifying affected existing bookings. The buffer-change report currently compares bookings only.

requirements.name: Equipment request management
requirements.intent: Coordinator requests route to Tech Support with quantities and notes; invalid multi-item writes roll back; reservation-derived status agrees with actual allocations.

requirements.name: Equipment availability checking
requirements.intent: Overlapping stock reservations reduce availability; touching windows do not; damaged/maintenance stock is unavailable.

requirements.name: Equipment reservation
requirements.intent: Allocations reduce shared stock, remain event-associated, reject stale revisions/over-reservation and roll back every item on a failed allocation.

requirements.name: Attendee registration
requirements.intent: Attendees register once within capacity, retain their own receipt, and withdraw under the saved policy; competing final-place/withdrawal requests cannot duplicate capacity. Only the owning Organiser and current assigned Coordinator can read the event roster and event-wide registration totals.

checks.test: sees names, references and event-wide totals across pages and filters

gaps: SCRUM-45 renders and counts Waitlisted, but real waiting-list records and promotion remain deferred SCRUM-80; the current schema only stores Registered and Withdrawn. Non-zero waitlisted presentation is controlled-browser evidence, not a live waitlist journey.
TC-43-02 waiting-list promotion remains deferred SCRUM-80; do not mark it passed. Owner must reconcile that documented case with the agreed release slice.
Registration closes when safety approval moves to Preparation; owner must verify the customer accepts that signup window.

requirements.name: Event change requests
requirements.intent: The Organiser raises a request without silently editing the event; assigned Coordinator reviews it with audit and notifications; outsiders cannot act.
gaps: SCRUM-138/152/156/48/166 apply significant changes, preserve resources and return Confirmed/Preparation date changes to Planning. Other significant changes remain flag-only under D36/D43/D64; final policy acceptance remains human-owned.

requirements.name: Notifications
requirements.intent: Private and role-pool notifications reach only their intended readers; key request/assignment/booking/registration outcomes are emitted.
gaps: Audit A4 (3 November 2026): confirmation writes status/history/notification separately; notification failure can return 503 after confirmation and retry is refused. A complete trigger-by-recipient and failure-recovery matrix remains outstanding.
Attendee venue-change notices are explicitly deferred by Marcus in D57/SCRUM-165; date/time and cancellation notices remain in scope. Reconcile SCRUM-51 description with that recorded scope decision.
Hold-expiry notice persistence limitations remain under W7-04; passing mocked sweep tests do not establish a real browser/API/database notification journey.

requirements.name: Venue setup and turnaround buffers
requirements.intent: Venue setup/turnaround expand occupied windows; touching expanded boundaries remain non-conflicting; newly conflicting existing bookings are flagged.
gaps: Audit A3 (3 November 2026): increasing buffers can introduce a conflict with pre-existing maintenance without identifying/notifying affected existing bookings. The buffer-change report currently compares bookings only.

requirements.name: Venue becomes unavailable after booking
requirements.intent: Venue Staff mark temporary unavailability with reason, retain affected events, notify Coordinators, and support replacement venue arrangements.

checks.test: Venue Staff can create and unblock a venue period
-only maintenance notifies and supports a replacement

gaps: Audit A3 (3 November 2026): increasing buffers can introduce a conflict with pre-existing maintenance without identifying/notifying affected existing bookings. The buffer-change report currently compares bookings only.

Block creation and coordinator notifications use separate writes (D66). Persistence-failure recovery remains a documented limitation; concurrency enforcement does not prove atomic notification delivery.

requirements.name: Multiple venues per event
requirements.intent: One event owns independent venue bookings; sibling edits/cancellations are isolated and confirmation requires all active venues approved.

checks.test: Coordinator changes one Requested booking and the changes survive reopening

requirements.name: Expiring tentative venue holds
requirements.intent: A hold has a future expiry before event start; exact-deadline expiry releases availability and must notify the Coordinator.
gaps: Audit A1 (3 November 2026): an Expired historical hold is treated as pending by event confirmation, so even an approved replacement cannot unblock confirmation. Add an integrated expiry-to-replacement-to-confirmation regression after fixing the gate.

Expiry uses an opportunistic application sweep and a database trigger (D58), not a scheduler. Sweep notice tests use controlled dependencies; trigger-only releases and notification failures do not establish reliable persisted notice delivery.

requirements.name: Event Coordinator Lead
requirements.intent: Lead assigns/reassigns from the unassigned queue. Coordinator list visibility is broader than permission to open/edit another Coordinator event, per D28.
gaps: Week 7 original own-events wording and later SCRUM-54 view-all decision require final owner acceptance of D28; list visibility must not be presented as edit permission.
PR #101 leaves Lead access to booking records unresolved. Direct booking read/change/cancel endpoints exclude the Lead; widening access requires an explicit owner decision and authorization review.

requirements.name: Operational safety check
requirements.owner: Marcus; Jerome for Safety Officer access
requirements.intent: Safety Officer sees scoped resource details and approves Confirmed to Preparation or sends back with a reason. Other roles cannot bypass the gate.
gaps: Audit A2 (3 November 2026): cancelling the only confirmed venue booking leaves the event Confirmed and the safety endpoint can approve Preparation without rechecking current resources.

SCRUM-128 requires emergency access, crowd movement, restrictions and equipment placement information. Current UI prompts and catalogue equipment location do not establish event-specific detail; owner acceptance or additional implementation remains required.

reviewed_against: Reconciled 3 November 2026 against main 9b7973b: merged PRs #101/#102/#103/#104/#107; retain audit A1-A4 and unresolved acceptance decisions. Evidence replay is not a new full-suite execution or release acceptance.
